status_definitions.derivation_checked: Local mathematical derivation checked by author and independent reviewer under the written hypotheses.
status_definitions.external_statement_checked: The stated theorem/convention was checked in the pinned primary source; the external proof was not re-refereed.
status_definitions.conditional_external_statement_checked: A preprint statement was checked in its pinned source; it is retained only as an explicit hypothetical input.
status_definitions.exact_finite_check: Exact rational/algebraic arithmetic checks the stated finite fixture, not transcendental evaluation or an asymptotic theorem.
status_definitions.numerical_check: Finite numerical evidence tied to its own source/result and measured residuals; no interval certification or asymptotic conclusion.
status_definitions.conditional_bound: A proved implication under an error or analytic hypothesis not established by the finite computation.
status_definitions.reported_unreplayed: Historical implementation or precision/sensitivity report remains unrecovered; any reproduced numerical values are identified separately.
status_definitions.open_target: An unproved target or unverified geometric instantiation, not a publication-ready theorem.

claims.scope: The gauge is positively homogeneous, its shortest nonzero lattice value is one, and counts include the boundary and exclude zero. All primitive vectors are counted with signs.
hypotheses: B is a fixed convex body with zero in its interior.
claims.proof_notes: Central symmetry is unnecessary for the general discrepancy arguments; the torus curve count is half the signed count.

claims.scope: Exact primitive inversion and the normalized signed harmonic sum; the omitted area tail is uniformly bounded after division by L.
hypotheses: L>=2; M=floor(L).
claims.proof_notes: Each nonzero lattice vector has a unique positive gcd and signed primitive part. A0(u)=0 for u<1. L*sum(d^-2,d>M)<=L/M<=2.

finite_computation.limit: Exact finite rational examples only; no geometric modulus, infinite-range bound or arithmetic hypothesis is established.

claims.scope: Absolute values and the decreasing envelope give L times one plus the logarithmic modulus integral.
hypotheses: omega(u)=sup(v>=u)|D(v)|/v.
claims.proof_notes: For d<=floor(L)-1 integrate over [L/(d+1),L/d]; log(1+1/d)>=1/(2d). Treat the last interval below one by the bounded boundary discrepancy.

claims.scope: An integrable normalized envelope gives O_B(L) without arithmetic cancellation; any fixed all-point power saving implies this hypothesis.
hypotheses: Integral of omega(u)/u from one to infinity is finite.
claims.proof_notes: The example exp(-sqrt(log u)) has finite logarithmic integral but no fixed power decay. PNT supplies the separate o(L) improvement in s31.dini_pnt.

claims.scope: Each chord-length function has a zero extension in W^{1,1} and derivative norm at most twice diam(B).
hypotheses: B is strictly convex, compact, with nonempty interior.
claims.proof_notes: Concavity, endpoint singleton support, local absolute continuity and total variation give the endpoint extension. No smoothness or curvature lower bound is assumed.

claims.scope: Along each fixed ray r*Fourier(1_B)(r nu) tends to zero; its absolute value is uniformly bounded in the direction.
hypotheses: Fourier convention exp(-2*pi*i*x.xi).
claims.proof_notes: Fubini followed by integration by parts and Riemann-Lebesgue. Directionwise convergence, not a uniform directional rate, is used.

claims.scope: Fixed-radius mollification, Poisson summation and a convex-body sandwich prove D_B(L)=o_B(L).
hypotheses: Choose r0 disk contained in B and a fixed nonnegative smooth unit-mass mollifier supported in epsilon disk.
claims.proof_notes: After division by L, nonzero Fourier terms have the summable majorant C*|m|^-1*|rhohat_epsilon(m)|. First send L to infinity at fixed epsilon, then epsilon to zero. Excluding the origin changes the count by one.

claims.scope: Strict convexity gives omega(u)->0 and E_primitive(L)=o_B(L log L), with no effective rate.
The rational-polygon upper bound and origin-star-shaped rational-polygon Omega_± lower bound apply to polygons, not automatically to strictly convex norm balls.
hypotheses: Rational vertices; the lower theorem additionally requires origin-star-shapedness.

claims.scope: At integer N>=1 the signed primitive count in [-N,N]^2 is 8*sum(phi(n),n<=N).
hypotheses: Closed square; zero excluded.
claims.proof_notes: Partition by the maximum absolute coordinate; the N=1 shell also has eight points.

finite_computation.limit: Exact finite rational examples only; no geometric modulus, infinite-range bound or arithmetic hypothesis is established.

claims.scope: A fixed area error delta_a creates delta_a*L^2 main-term error; error o(L) requires area discrepancy o(1/L) and boundary membership control.
hypotheses: This is a necessary accuracy comparison, not a sufficient lattice approximation theorem.

claims.scope: Telescoping inversion removes c exactly and gives the stated O(L) and O(L log L) equivalences.
hypotheses: N(L)/L^2 tends to a fixed c; E=N-cL^2.
claims.proof_notes: At k steps the remaining term is 4^-k E(2^k L), which tends to zero. Under each displayed bound the inverse series converges absolutely. Finite blocks do not supply the infinite-range hypothesis.

claims.scope: All full/half events, grouped simultaneous jumps, one-sided limits and exact segment integrals determine the finite M/Q metrics.
hypotheses: Locally finite positive lengths with multiplicities; N counts <=L; [T,2T] needs the spectrum through 4T.
claims.proof_notes: Full events jump by -4; half events by +1. Exclude the external left limit at T, include both limits at the terminal endpoint. Integral is D^2*(1/a-1/b).

claims.scope: The row intersection at T=L+delta has the displayed endpoints and width T*W(h*delta/T).
hypotheses: B strictly convex and contains zero; unique top point (alpha,h), h>0; alpha/h irrational; two-sided local upper graph over an open x interval; L=n/h; delta>0 and delta=o(L).
claims.proof_notes: The local profile is convex, uniquely minimized at zero, and strictly increasing on each side. Its inverses are concave. Compactness ensures sufficiently shallow caps lie in this local graph.

claims.scope: For prime n the new row contains w+O(1) primitive lattice points with lower bound w-2.
hypotheses: The row width is eventually <n; alpha/h is irrational.
claims.proof_notes: The contact row has no lattice point. An interval shorter than n contains at most one multiple of n; all other integers are coprime to n.

claims.scope: Monotone inclusion of the dilates turns a primitive-row burst into the displayed two-scale discrepancy lower bound.
hypotheses: Same contact and prime-row hypotheses.
claims.proof_notes: No points disappear because zero lies inside B; subtract c_B*(2L delta+delta^2), then max absolute values is at least half the positive difference.

claims.scope: At delta=1/L, concavity gives w>=L W(h/L^2), while the quadratic main term changes by O_B(1). The figure is schematic.
claims.proof_notes: W(h/(L^2+1)) >= L^2/(L^2+1)*W(h/L^2). The product with L+1/L cancels exactly.

claims.scope: An explicitly infinitely flat graph gives W(u)>>_N u^(1/N), hence Omega(L^(1-epsilon)) for every epsilon>0 along contact scales; not Omega(L).
hypotheses: For every N, f(±s)<=C_N*s^N near zero, in addition to the supporting-row hypotheses.
claims.proof_notes: W(u)->0 under strict convexity, so this single microscopic row gives only o(L) as its own lower-bound scale.

claims.scope: The three model inversions give L/(log L)^(1/beta), L/(log log L)^(1/beta), and L*exp(-(2 log L)^(1/gamma)), respectively.
hypotheses: Model inequalities hold two-sided locally; beta>0, gamma>1; use the contact hypotheses for discrepancy implications.
claims.proof_notes: Each displayed profile has positive second derivative sufficiently near zero. Matching upper/lower graph profiles determine row width, not the total discrepancy. None is identified as an actual torus profile.

claims.scope: The divisor sum counts closed-interval coprime integers exactly, including negative and integer endpoints; its error from width*phi(n)/n is O(2^omega(n)).
hypotheses: n>=1 integer; real a<=b.
claims.proof_notes: Use sum(mu(d),d|gcd(k,n)) and count multiples in [a,b]. Each squarefree-divisor rounding error is bounded by one.
